subject: Urgent: HealthSpan latency & error spike — KV lane congestion suspected
messages:
From: Alexandre Dupont <alexandre.dupont@healthspan.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@healthspan.com>
Date: Tue, 04 Dec 2028 16:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: sudden latency spike — urgent

Rachel —

We started seeing a big jump in API p99 and 500s this morning around 10:20 PST. Topline: p50 is fine, but p99 jumped from ~450ms to 3.2s and 5xx rate climbed to ~4.8% across our production keys. Throughput reported to us via your dashboard also dropped ~30% for our tenant. No change on our side.

We noticed the timing correlates with a Redwood platform rollout this morning (you may have a canary running?). The errors are impacting our support queue; customers are getting timeouts. Can you confirm what changed and how quickly this can be mitigated?

Attached: short log tail and a screenshot from our monitoring (they show the spike and traces).

— Alexandre
Customer Success Lead
HealthSpan Analytics
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Alexandre Dupont <alexandre.dupont@healthspan.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 04 Dec 2028 17:02:12 +0000
Subject: Re: sudden latency spike — urgent

Alexandre — thanks for the flag and the logs, we see the same on our side.

Short acknowledgement and immediate actions:
- I’ve opened an incident and routed to SRE (Ben & Naomi cc’d).
- Can you confirm whether this affects all API keys or a subset? Your logs look tenant-wide.
- We’re going to pause a small config canary (if currently active) and roll back the prefix-store TTL change that went out in the 05:30 UTC deployment.

I’ll keep you updated every 30 mins until stable.

R
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Lead — Redwood Inference
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 04 Dec 2028 17:08:33 +0000
Subject: [Internal] HealthSpan — suspected KV cache thrash / HOL blocking (initial triage)

Team —

Recap: HealthSpan reports p99 ~3.2s, 5xx ~4.8%, throughput drop ~30%. Timeline aligns with this morning’s runtime config push (05:30 UTC) which included a prefix-store TTL reduction and some new prefetch heuristics.

Preliminary findings from quick look:
- Prefetch hit rate for HealthSpan’s tenant dropped from ~82% -> ~38% starting 05:32 UTC.
- KV cache evictions spiked dramatically; eviction rate +220% for the tenant’s hot shards.
- Hot-lane (priority) queueing shows lane starvation: batch lane utilization is maxed while other lanes are idle — classic HOL blocking when hot keys thrash the small hot-key pool.
- There are ~3 keys accounting for ~47% of requests; recent TTL tweak aggressively reclaimed those entries leading to repeated expensive recomputations and KV churn.

Immediate mitigation plan (we can do in parallel):
1) Roll back the prefix-store TTL change for HealthSpan (rollback queued, will take effect in next 2 minutes).
2) Temporarily pin top-3 hot keys for their tenant to a reserved hot-key slot (reduce eviction pressure).
3) Increase tenant kv_cache_capacity by +40% for next 60 minutes and monitor.
4) Disable the new prefetch heuristic for this tenant (it’s under canary).
5) If p99 doesn't fall within 15 minutes after 1–3, expand to a full canary rollback.

Requests: Ben — can SRE apply 1–3 now (scripts exist in ops-scripts/kv-adjust)? Naomi — please run a focused flamegraph/trace aggregation for the 10:20–10:40 window and share results. Jonas — FYI and I’ll need approval for a one-off customer credit request if this extends beyond 2 hours.

Quoted for context:
> On Tue, Dec 4, 2028 at 16:45 Alexandre Dupont <alexandre.dupont@healthspan.com> wrote:
> > We started seeing a big jump in API p99 and 500s this morning around 10:20 PST....

R
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 05 Dec 2028 01:12:05 +0000
Subject: Exec: HealthSpan SLA impact / credit approval request

Rachel —

Thanks for the write-up. If mitigation doesn’t restore steady state within 2 hours we should approve a goodwill credit to preserve the account — recommend up to 20% off their monthly bill for this cycle and a technical review session (post-mortem) with the account team.

Operational ask: prioritize rollback & pinning as you outlined. If we see repeated hot-key thrash for the same tenant over 24–72 hours, we need to offer either a dedicated lane (reserved capacity) or a configuration change to their prefixing strategy — discuss with Solutions.

Please update with candidate timeline for resolution; I’ll notify Sales Ops and Finance if we pull the credit trigger.

— Jonas
VP, Customer Reliability
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alexandre Dupont <alexandre.dupont@healthspan.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 05 Dec 2028 19:12:00 +0000
Subject: HealthSpan — status update and immediate fixes applied

Alexandre — quick update from the ops side:

What we did (completed):
- Rolled back prefix-store TTL change for HealthSpan at 2028-12-05T17:03:12Z (rollback id rb-20281205-17).
- Pinned top-3 hot keys to reserved slots for the tenant to prevent eviction thrash.
- Increased kv_cache_capacity for the tenant by +40% for a 60-minute window (monitoring in place).
- Disabled the canary prefetch heuristic for HealthSpan.

Observed effect (first 25 minutes):
- Prefetch hit rate recovered from ~38% -> ~79%.
- p99 reduced from ~3.2s -> ~480ms.
- 5xx rate dropped from ~4.8% -> ~0.4%.
- Throughput recovered to ~95% of baseline.

Attachments: dashboard snapshot (attached) and short support log tail for the failure window. We’ll keep the pinning and capacity increase for now and will start a controlled test to see if pinning alone suffices.

Next steps:
- Naomi to hand off detailed trace and flamegraphs in the incident doc (drive link sent).
- Rachel to coordinate post-mortem and customer credit if Jonas signs off.
- Product to add tenant-level hot-key pinning as an on-demand remediation knob in the console (proposal to follow).

Ben Carter
SRE — Redwood Inference

--
